To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the combination of cyclophosphamide, doxorubicin, cisplatin, and prednisone (CAP) is highly effective in the treatment of metastatic breast cancer, and that dose intensification of this combination using high-dose alkylating agents with autologous bone-marrow support is safe, and can be associated with long-term disease-free survival and even cure.
the addition of a bone marrow transplant to dose intensification with alkylating agents in patients with breast cancer is not associated with an improved outcome.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new approaches for the treatment of metastatic breast cancer.
the development of new therapeutic approaches to the treatment of metastatic breast cancer.
the development of new therapeutic regimens in the treatment of metastatic breast cancer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the current treatment of metastatic breast cancer, even when administered in combination, has failed to produce a cure in the majority of patients and has not improved the median duration of survival or time to treatment failure.
there is no effective therapy available for the majority of patients with metastatic disease.
the treatment of metastatic breast cancer with combination chemotherapy regimens remains largely palliative, although some patients may experience prolonged survival.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the use of dose intensification using combination chemotherapy with autologous bone-marrow support has resulted in a 2- to 3-fold increase in complete response rate in both primary breast cancer and breast cancer metastatic to bone marrow.
dose intensification of alkylating agents using autologous bone-marrow support is a promising approach to the treatment of metastatic breast cancer and warrants further investigation.

dose intensity is an important determinant in the treatment of metastatic breast cancer, and dose intensification using combination chemotherapy regimens and autologous marrow support may be a means to achieve higher complete response rates and prolong survival in patients with metastatic disease.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there is a significant difference between the number of people who have breast cancer and those who have metastatic breast cancer.
the combination of the two drugs, when given in the proper sequence and at the right doses, is more effective than either drug alone.
there is a significant benefit to dose intensifying therapy in patients with metastatic disease, and the benefit is greatest in those who have received no prior therapy.
